name: Jana Small Finance Bank Ltd
title: Jana Small Finance Bank Ltd - 544118 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 record PBT and PAT guidance raised to 100% growth, but deposits (17% YoY) and CASA lag the 23-25% guide; credit cost guided below 2% with the CGFMU guarantee claims as a key dependency.

triggers.label: PAT growth guide raised 80% → 100%

triggers.label: Cost of funds 7.9% → 7.4% YoY
triggers.quote: cost of funds is down from 7.9% to 7.4%.

triggers.label: CASA growth 13%, below plan
triggers.quote: Year-on-year CASA growth is 13%, TD is 17.5%. We have work to do on CASA

triggers.label: Credit cost peaked; H1 0.92%
triggers.quote: the credit cost in a way has peaked out in Q2.

guidance.quote: we would like to take our guidance up, which was originally increase of 80% in PAT to 100% of PAT.
While we are maintaining the guidance for both advances and deposits at 19% to 21% for advances and 23% to 25% for deposits.
I would still stick to my 23% to 25% deposit growth rate.
I do want to keep my cost of funds around where it is today.
Overall, certainly below 2%. I think that was the most important point here.
Will it go below 60, I think it's achievable, but I would be cautious in saying this year likelihood probably is low.
Gold, on the other hand, should go back to its 30%, 40% growth rate, which means about 10% a quarter comfortably from Q3

summary.headline: Jana SFB raised FY27 PAT growth guidance to 100% (from 80%) after Q2 posted its highest-ever PBT; H1 PAT of INR 326 crore equals full-year FY26 PAT.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the bank's highest-ever quarterly PBT, with H1 PAT of INR 326 crore equal to FY26 full-year PAT. NIM rose to 7.54% from 6.5% a year ago and cost of funds fell to 7.4% from 7.9%. Gross NPA improved to 2.17% but net NPA rose to 1.08%, which management expects to fall below 1% once INR 68 crore of CGFMU guarantee claims are realised. Advances grew 22% YoY to INR 38,752 crore, while CASA growth of 13% YoY lagged deposits at 17.5% TD growth and remains a focus area.

financial_highlights.change: down from 7.9% in Q2 FY26; stable QoQ
expected below 1% after INR 68 crore guarantee claim realisation
opex up 15% YoY; positive jaws of about 20%

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Largest secured book, growing 28.2% YoY with average ticket size INR 11.9 lakh; operates in about 220 cities with roughly 3,000 people in business roles.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Growing 20.6% YoY; management guides 25-30% growth for this year and next, citing PLI and Make in India demand.

segments.name: Vehicle loans (2-wheeler and used car)
segments.commentary: Grew 76% YoY; 2-wheelers offered in 135 cities and used cars in 50 cities; Q3 expected to be strongest on Diwali demand.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Up 81% YoY but only 0.3% QoQ; 65-70% of the Jan-Mar 2026 6-month loans came up for renewal in Q2. Management expects growth of about 10% a quarter from Q3.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Growth slowed to about 3% (management expects 7-8% at best); no loosening of credit criteria.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: Now 26% of gross loan book; collections at 99% including BC book; growth subdued given weak bureau histories among borrowers. 97% of customers have two or fewer MFI lenders vs 93% industry.

segments.name: Unsecured advances
segments.commentary: Up 17% YoY but down 0.3% QoQ; all new disbursements placed under the CGFMU guarantee programme. Uncovered gross NPA of INR 296 crore sits under guarantee cover of INR 319 crore.

segments.name: NBFC term loans
segments.commentary: Growth of 0.7% YoY; management does not expect significant growth.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: CASA up 13% YoY; TD up 17.5% YoY; 96.1% of deposits have contractual tenor of 1 year and above.

guidance_outlook: PAT growth guidance raised to 100% YoY for FY27 from earlier 80%; management expects H2 PAT at least equal to H1 for this to hold.
Advances growth guidance maintained at 19-21%; deposit growth guidance maintained at 23-25%.
Full-year credit cost expected below 2%; H2 credit cost expected lower than H1's 0.92%.
Secured share of book expected to reach about 75% by year-end, versus 73.7% at Q2 and a long-term target of about 80%.
Cost-to-income targeted toward 60% over coming quarters; management says FY27 achievement is unlikely, with 57% (March 2024 level) as the first goal.
NIM expected to stay around current levels (about 7.5%) in H2 with cost of funds around 7.4%.
Guarantee claims of INR 68 crore expected to be received within about 2 months (by end-November); remaining INR 251 crore to be lodged in Q3 next year.

Branch expansion: 78 branches planned, 40 opened so far; launches planned for credit line on UPI (Q2 proof of concept), loans against shares and mutual funds (November), and trade FX via AD-1 licence (December).
capex_capacity: About 820 branches across India; 78 branch openings planned for FY27, with 40 completed by the call date.
Digital onboarding for non-face-to-face CASA accounts expected by January.
AI-led processes introduced in collections, welcome calling and cross-sell, reducing headcount and cost.
Headcount in September 2026 lower than March 2026 despite asset and liability growth.
demand_pricing: Q2 disbursements of INR 4,414 crore, up 7% YoY and 5% QoQ.
Affordable housing average ticket size INR 11.9 lakh; top seven states make up 67% of concentration, top three 37%.
Insurance income for H1 about INR 45 crore; 80-90% linked to credit life and 10-20% to retail products. IRDAI consultation impact not yet fully assessed.
Management says deposit pricing is fairly competitive; interest rates were harder in Q2 than Q1 and the market shows no sign of weakening rate regime.
Customers in the petroleum supply chain and related MSMEs show marginal impact; some export-linked sourcing paused because of higher shipping costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will slippages trend up or down in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower slippages in Q3 and H2. Q2 had one-offs: a secured loan slippage adding about 0.2% and drought-related MFI slippage of about 0.3%. SMA has graduated down in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 insurance income is credit life and what is the IRDAI consultation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: 80-90% is credit life, 10-20% retail products. Initial IRDAI assessment done; full assessment pending. Management will push penetration and AI-led cost efficiency to offset lower commissions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cost-to-income decline sustainable and can it fall below 60%?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost-to-income expected to stay at or below the September level; management is cautious that sub-60% is unlikely this year. Drivers are productivity, RPA/AI processes and more direct sourcing over DSA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CASA outlook and cost of funds risk from rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: CASA fell 2% QoQ in ratio terms but grew 13% YoY; management targets about 20% CASA in H2 via affluent offers and digital onboarding by January. Cost of funds targeted to stay near 7.4%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the guarantee scheme cover the full book and what if it does not?
qa_highlights.answer: Claims of INR 68 crore lodged; NGC expected to pay within about 2 months. CGFMU is not open for fresh guarantees yet, but 1% cover cost has been accrued. If the scheme fails, the accrual becomes a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gold loan and micro LAP flat, and when will growth pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold flat due to 6-month loans from Jan-Mar 2026 renewing in Q2 and gold price drop; growth expected to resume in Q3 at about 10% a quarter. Micro LAP may reach 7-8% growth but not much more.

qa_highlights.question: Any risks to achieving 100% PAT growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no visible constraint on H2 profit matching H1; credit costs, asset growth and liability growth were all cited as on track.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM move in H2 amid rising rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects NIM around current levels, as MFI share is not rising faster and secured share only reaches about 75%; cost of funds should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook by segment and do drought and geopolitical risks affect the book?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME 25-30% growth, affordable housing and vehicles continue strongly. Drought declared in 29 Karnataka districts and 34 Maharashtra districts; slippage impact expected to be immaterial. No material impact from the Iran war so far.

risks_watch: CGFMU guarantee scheme not yet open for fresh guarantees; if it does not reopen, the INR 296 crore uncovered unsecured NPA and future MFI risk rest on the bank's own buffer.
Net NPA at 1.08% is above the 1% comfort level until the INR 68 crore claim is received, expected by end-November.
CASA ratio fell and CASA growth (13% YoY) trails TD growth; deposit growth of 17% YoY is below the 23-25% guidance.
Drought in Karnataka and Maharashtra may lift slippages and moratorium requests; geopolitical oil and shipping cost impact on MSME exporters.

IRDAI insurance commission consultation could cut non-interest income; full impact not yet assessed. Media speculation about a merger, which management said it would evaluate if strategically sensible.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, asset quality and cost trajectory, with raised PAT guidance. Management is cautious and candid on CASA, deposit growth shortfall, gold and micro LAP growth, and the cost-to-income target, which it says is unlikely to reach 60% this year.
key_quotes: Q2 has been the highest ever PBT we had in our history.
So rather than provision now and then work around the whole accounting system next quarter again once this claim comes, we have chosen that we will go to 1.08%.
CASA is not our strength at this point of time, and we are doing everything which is possibly available in our heads and efforts to make sure that we bring it up.
I don't see a challenge in the asset growth piece because our products have been in the market for the last 7, 8 years and we've met with good success.

adds.what: 78 branch openings planned for FY27 (about 820 branches total); 40 opened so far

growth.why: PAT growth guidance raised to 100% for FY27 from 80%, with advances guided at 19-21% and deposits at 23-25%; backing is partial (40 of 78 branches opened, H1 PAT of INR 326 crore, guarantee-covered disbursements), but no capacity or order figures tie the raised PAT target to specific drivers.
